extraction.name: EuroSAT
extraction.description: A land use and land cover classification dataset containing 27,000 labeled and geo-referenced Sentinel-2 satellite image patches measuring 64x64 pixels. It covers 13 spectral bands and 10 classes, with 2,000 to 3,000 images per class. RGB and multispectral versions are released.
extraction.creator: Patrick Helber; Benjamin Bischke; Andreas Dengel; Damian Borth
extraction.citeAs: Patrick Helber, Benjamin Bischke, Andreas Dengel, Damian Borth. EuroSAT: A Novel Dataset and Deep Learning Benchmark for Land Use and Land Cover Classification. arXiv:1709.00029v2 [cs.CV], 1 February 2019.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The authors downloaded Sentinel-2A satellite images via Amazon S3, selecting images associated with cities covered by the European Urban Atlas across 34 European countries. Images with low cloud levels were selected using ESA-provided cloud percentage values. Images recorded throughout the year were extracted to increase within-class variation. From these images, the authors created 27,000 geo-referenced and labeled 64x64-pixel patches and manually checked them multiple times.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Secondary Data analysis, Manual Human Curator
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Multispectral imagery acquired by the Sentinel-2A satellite's Multispectral Imager under ESA's Copernicus Earth observation program, downloaded through Amazon S3. The imagery covers 13 spectral bands with native spatial resolutions of 10, 20, or 60 meters per pixel. Geographic image selection was based on cities covered by the European Urban Atlas.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: The authors extracted 64x64-pixel patches from satellite images. For RGB benchmarking, they combined red (B04), green (B03), and blue (B02) bands. For single-band evaluation, information from one spectral band was replicated across all three input channels. Shortwave-infrared and color-infrared band combinations were also evaluated.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Satellite images were selected for low cloud coverage. All patches were manually checked multiple times, and mislabeled images and images full of snow or ice were discarded. Discarded examples also included patches obscured by clouds or affected by dead pixels. No atmospheric correction was applied; images with atmospheric color casts were deliberately retained so the classifier could learn these cases. For spectral-band evaluation, lower-resolution bands were upsampled to 10 meters per pixel using cubic-spline interpolation.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Each image patch has a land use or land cover label from one of 10 classes: annual crop, permanent crop, pasture, highway, residential buildings, industrial buildings, river, sea & lake, forest, and herbaceous vegetation. Classes were chosen because they were visible at 10 meters per pixel and sufficiently represented in the European Urban Atlas to generate thousands of patches. Class composition and relationships follow the European Urban Atlas mapping guide; the residential class was created using its urban fabric classes. The authors manually checked all 27,000 images multiple times and corrected the ground truth by removing mislabeled images.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Ground-truth quality was checked through repeated manual review of all images. Mislabeled patches were removed rather than retained. No annotator disagreement or uncertainty analysis is described.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The paper describes applications in urban development, nature protection, and sustainable development. Land cover change detection can identify deforestation, which the paper identifies as a major contributor to climate change, and can help notice illegal forest clearing. The trained classification system can also assist in keeping crowdsourced geographical maps such as OpenStreetMap up to date.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The geographic distribution is influenced by the number of cities represented per country in the European Urban Atlas. Classes were selected for visibility at 10-meter resolution and sufficient frequency in the European Urban Atlas. Low-cloud imagery was preferentially selected, and patches full of snow or ice were excluded.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The dataset has not received atmospheric correction, which can result in color casts, including extreme cases retained in the dataset. A classification system trained on 64x64-pixel patches does not allow finely graduated per-pixel segmentation. Detailed analysis of land areas requires high-resolution satellite imagery and an advanced segmentation approach.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Training, testing, fine-tuning, and benchmarking land use and land cover image classifiers, including deep convolutional neural networks. The paper evaluates different training-test splits and uses a class-wise 80/20 split for comparative benchmarking. The dataset supports spectral-band evaluation, land use and land cover change detection, and assistance with geographical mapping, including verification of tagged areas, identification of mistagged areas, and large-area tagging.
